did_you_know.text: Did you know? Psalm 86 opens with the title “A Prayer of David,” and the psalmist calls out to the Lord from a place of poverty and need: “For I am poor and needy.”
Did you know? The psalmist asks the Lord to guard his life and describes himself as devoted and trusting in the Lord, whom he calls “my God.”
Did you know? The psalm says that the Lord’s goodness, forgiveness, and abundant mercy are available “to all who call on you”—to everyone who calls out to him.
Did you know? The psalmist declares that he will call on the Lord in the day of his trouble because he is confident that the Lord will answer him.
Did you know? The psalm emphasizes the Lord’s uniqueness with the question and declaration: “There is none like you among the gods” and “there are no works like yours.”
Did you know? The psalm envisions all the nations the Lord has made coming to bow down before him and honor his name.
Did you know? The psalmist asks not only for deliverance but also for guidance: to learn the Lord’s way, walk in his truth, and unite his heart to fear his name.
Did you know? After asking for guidance, the psalmist promises to thank the Lord with all his heart and honor his name forever.
Did you know? In contrast to the arrogant and ruthless, the psalmist highlights the Lord’s qualities: compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, and rich in steadfast love and faithfulness.
Did you know? At the end of the psalm, the psalmist asks for “a sign of your favor”—a sign that will express the Lord’s help and comfort and cause his enemies to see it and be put to shame.
